algorithm.title: Evaluation and Management of Metatarsal Fractures

cell.label: Take history to determine mechanism of injury; evaluate neurovascular status. Inspect skin for ecchymosis, abrasions, swelling, tenting, deformity. Apply Ottawa Foot Rule. Radiography recommended?
Palpate for point tenderness based on patient complaint and apply axial load to metatarsal head.
Consider alternative diagnosis (eg, soft tissue injury).
Posterior splint, nonweight-bearing, follow-up in 3-5 d, then SLNWBC.
Follow-up in 7-10 d and repeat radiographs. Continue cast for 3-4 wk, progressive weight bearing.
Elastic dressing or hard shoe and progressive weight bearing. Follow-up in 3-5 d. Repeat radiographs in 1 wk and again in 4-6 wk.
Manage as per displaced (if single metatarsal fracture).
History of recent increase in activity?
If tender to palpation near T-MT, rule out Lisfranc fracture. Obtain weight-bearing films, CT, MRI.

footnotes.footnote: Data from Stiell IG, Greenberg GH, McKnight RD, et al. Clinical prediction rules for the use of radiography in acute ankle injuries. Refinement and prospective validation. JAMA 1993;269:1127-1132.

algorithm.title: Suspected Proximal Fifth Metatarsal Fracture: Management.

cell.label: Determine fracture location relative to 4th-5th intermetatarsal articulation.
Soft protective dressing Weight bearing as tolerated.
Displaced? OR Prompt return to athletics desired?
Posterior splint for 3-5 days; then SLNWBC for 6-8 wk. This is followed by hard shoe or walking cast until symptomatic and radiographic healing.
Type I (early), type II (delayed), or type III (nonunion)?
SLNWBC until healed. Nonunion after 8-12 wk?
